sources.title: Quantum Information Processing course notes, QIC 710 / CS 768 / PHYS 767 / CO 681 / AMATH 871 / PMATH 871
sources.locator: Complete official 328-page QIC 710 F26 notes; §§37.1–37.3, printed pp.292–303; PDF pp.300–311.

contents.name: §37.1.1–37.1.3: binary duals, generator/parity-check matrices, syndrome and distance argument
contents.reason: The note supplies the standard binary pairing and syndrome route; the carrier proves dual dimension locally by coordinate duality, finite basis extension, and rank-nullity.

contents.name: §§37.2–37.3.1: Walsh–Hadamard transform of subspace and offset-coset states; CSS coset encoding
contents.reason: The carrier derives the full C2⊆C1 construction and its dual-basis Fourier formula locally. Cleve’s own CSS setup also assumes C0-perp⊆C1; that extra hypothesis is not imported into this item.

contents.name: §37.3.2: separate bit-flip and phase-flip syndrome procedures and the Steane construction
contents.reason: The note motivates separate decoders; the carrier derives each ancilla parity on basis inputs, label-independence, the conservative distance radius, and the KL extension locally.

contents.name: §37.3.1–37.3.2: Hamming and Steane code matrices and logical cosets
contents.reason: The carrier uses a different explicit column order and verifies its matrix ranks, code distance, logical operators, and every single-site syndrome locally.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 7: Quantum Error Correction
sources.locator: Complete 92-page Quantum Error Correction chapter; §§7.6–7.10, printed pp.19–34; PDF pp.25–40; §§7.18.1–7.18.5, printed pp.51–58; PDF pp.57–64.

contents.name: §§7.7–7.8: nested CSS codes, stabilizer checks, symplectic normalizer, Steane code and logical operators
contents.reason: The carrier states the standard Hermitian phase-aware convention explicitly and proves subgroup/projector interfaces locally; Preskill’s 2015 Y convention is anti-Hermitian, so only convention-independent structural context is used.

contents.name: §§7.7–7.8: CSS coset states, Hadamard dual basis, syndrome checks, and Steane example
contents.reason: The carrier states and proves the general nested-code convention with no additional C2-perp inclusion; the phase and label conventions are translated locally.

contents.name: §§7.10.1–7.10.4: stabilizer group, syndrome, binary symplectic form, distance and logical Pauli quotient
contents.reason: The source gives the normalizer/quotient route; the carrier proves the dimension calculation under the current phase-aware subgroup convention.

contents.name: §7.18.1–7.18.5: chain complexes, planar rough/smooth boundaries, relative paths, and surface-code distance context
contents.reason: The carrier specifies a relative d-by-d patch with rough left/right edges and proves all ranks, path classes, and counts locally; source boundary orientation is rotated and no diagram is used as proof.

contents.name: §§7.6–7.10: Steane code matrices and separate X/Z syndromes
contents.reason: All finite matrix checks and 21 syndrome values are recomputed locally.

sources.title: Eric Dennis, Alexei Kitaev, Andrew Landahl, and John Preskill, Topological quantum memory, Journal of Mathematical Physics 43 (2002), 4452–4505
sources.locator: Complete 54-page author-hosted PDF; §III.A–B, printed pp.4455–4461; PDF pp.4–10, especially the planar relative-cycle and shortest rough-to-rough / smooth-to-smooth path statements on printed pp.4460–4461 (PDF pp.9–10).

contents.name: §III.A: chain complexes, cycle versus boundary, normalizer versus stabilizer, and toric-code logical distance
contents.reason: This supports the chain-complex route; the item proves the relative-boundary patch ranks and its exact path count locally.

contents.name: §III.B: rough/smooth boundaries, relative cycles, encoded qubit count, and shortest boundary-to-boundary paths
contents.reason: The source is a second independent surface-code treatment. The local definition rotates rough edges to left/right and gives exact coordinate matrices and checks.

contents.name: §III.B: planar surface-code path distance and logical operators
contents.reason: The carrier proves the one-dimensional relative and dual quotients, exact distances d and d+1, and the (d+1)3^ell path bound from the specified finite grid.

sources.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6
sources.locator: Complete 239-page lecture notes; §20.1, printed p.173, PDF pp.185–186; §20.3, printed pp.175–176, PDF pp.187–188.

contents.name: §20.1: stabilizer states, phase-aware Pauli group and fixed-space dimension
contents.reason: The section gives the phase-aware Pauli and stabilizer-state convention. The local carriers handle arbitrary-rank code spaces and prove the full projector and quotient statements.

contents.name: §20.3: efficient simulation of Clifford circuits and Pauli measurement
contents.reason: This result concerns classical simulation of measurement-controlled Clifford circuits; QC20 proves a finite code encoder and its correctness, and imports no simulator or complexity claim.

sources.title: Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits, Physical Review A 70 (2004), arXiv:quant-ph/0406196v5
sources.locator: Complete 15-page paper; §II, phase-aware Pauli/stabilizer conventions, PDF pp.1–2; §VI, Lemmas 5–7, Theorem 8 and gate-count corollary, PDF pp.8–10.

contents.name: §II: phase-aware Pauli products and tableau representation
contents.reason: This treatment documents phase-aware tableaux and Clifford gate conventions. The local encoder states its own row operations and proves termination and correctness separately.

contents.name: §VI: canonical-form synthesis for unitary stabilizer circuits
contents.reason: The paper proves an 11-round circuit canonical form and its gate-count consequence; the local QC20 algorithm instead uses direct pivot elimination and proves only its own linear-size-per-pivot bound.
